abstract: The regulatory landscape of RNA includes diverse non-canonical 5' cap structures, including Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD+). In E. coli, the NAD cap and its cognate decapping enzyme NudC have provided important insight into NAD+-capped RNA stability; however, broader regulatory control of NAD-capped RNA degradation has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the E. coli Nudix hydrolase RppH, known to act on 5' triphosphorylated RNA, also functions as an NAD+-decapping enzyme. RppH removes NAD caps from both linear and structured (hairpin) RNA substrates, revealing a previously unrecognized role in NAD+-RNA metabolism. These findings suggest that RppH may function alongside NudC to regulate the stability of NAD-capped transcripts. We further establish a direct relationship between NAD-RNA turnover and the alarmone ppGpp. Quantitative inhibition assays demonstrate that ppGpp inhibits decapping of NAD+-RNA by both NudC and RppH and indicate coordinated regulation of NAD-RNA decay during stress conditions. To provide a structural basis for these observations, we determined crystal structures of NudC bound to NADH and ppGpp. These structures reveal that ppGpp occupies the NudC active site, supporting a competitive inhibition mechanism. Together, our findings identify RppH as a novel NAD+-decapping enzyme and establish ppGpp as a regulator of NAD-RNA decay pathways, linking RNA capping and metabolic stress signaling.
